title: Much Ado About Nothing — 30th Summer Season
excerpt: Join us June 10–28, 2026 at Pinkney Park for Shakespeare's sparkling comedy. VIP pre-sale April 7–14; general admission on sale April 15.
content:
Shakespeare on the Sound celebrates 30 seasons of storytelling under the stars with Much Ado About Nothing, directed by David Frederick Mold.

Shakespeare's sparkling comedy transports audiences to 19th-century Sicily, where romance blooms, tempers flare, and a battle of wits becomes a battle of hearts. Enjoy a brilliant ensemble in one of Connecticut's most beloved outdoor settings.

Performances run June 10–28, 2026 (no shows Mondays) at 7:30pm, Wednesdays through Sundays, at Pinkney Park, Rowayton, CT. Park opens at 5pm for blankets and chairs.

VIP reserved seating pre-sale: April 7–14. General admission tickets on sale beginning April 15. Adults $25, children 12 and under $5. Pay-What-You-Will performances Tuesday, June 16 and 23. Get tickets via Eventbrite or at the park box office during June.

title: Save the Date: Much Ado About Something Gala
excerpt: Friday, October 16, 2026, 6–10pm at The House Up on the Hill, 26 Seir Hill Rd., Norwalk, CT.
content:
Save the Date for our Much Ado About Something gala on Friday, October 16, 2026, 6–10pm at The House Up on the Hill, 26 Seir Hill Rd., Norwalk, CT.

Join us for a beautiful night of cocktails, delicious bites, dancing, and live and silent auctions in support of Shakespeare on the Sound. If you would like to join the committee for our fundraiser, contact contactus@shakespeareonthesound.org.

title: 2026 Season Sponsors Announced
excerpt: We thank DR Bank, Neil Hauck Architects, R+C, Russo & Rizio, Rowayton Seafood, and Fairfield County Bank for supporting our 30th season.
content:
Shakespeare on the Sound's 2026 summer production is made possible by generous community partners: DR Bank, Neil Hauck Architects, R+C, Russo & Rizio, Rowayton Seafood, and Fairfield County Bank.

Their support helps keep professional Shakespeare accessible under the stars at Pinkney Park and funds our year-round education programs across Fairfield County.

title: VIP Pre-Sale & General Tickets Now Available
excerpt: VIP reserved seating $75. General admission $25 adults / $5 children. Student & senior rush $15 at the box office day-of.
content:
VIP TICKETS PRE-SALE runs April 7–14. GENERAL ADMISSION TICKETS go on sale beginning April 15.

General admission: $25 adults, $5 children 12 and under (Wed–Sun evenings, June 10–28). VIP reserved seating any day: $75. Student and senior rush seating: $15 (65+ and current students, in person at the park box office day-of only).

Pay-What-You-Will Shakespeare: Tuesday, June 16 and 23 at 7:30pm (suggested donation $25 adults, $5 children). Apprentice Company matinee Saturday, June 20 at 1pm — walk-up admission only.

Special events include Opening Night reception (June 13), SOS Book Club (June 18), and Alumni Night (June 20). See our Productions page for full details.

title: Shakespeare for Kids in the Park
excerpt: Bring Shakespeare into your classroom and catch Shakespeare for kids in the park — including Shakespeare in 30 Minutes before select performances.
content:
Education is at the cornerstone of Shakespeare on the Sound. We provide workshops, touring shows, and summer camps across Fairfield County.

Visit our education tent in Pinkney Park before the show for Shakespeare in 30 Minutes — a family-friendly half-hour version of our MainStage production, 30 minutes before showtime.

For schools, libraries, and community programs, contact our education team at nick@shakespeareonthesound.org or stephanie@shakespeareonthesound.org.

title: Celebrating 30 Seasons in Rowayton
excerpt: Since 1996, Shakespeare on the Sound has brought professional outdoor Shakespeare to Pinkney Park — starting with Much Ado About Nothing.
content:
In 1996, Rowayton's 6th Taxing District gave permission for the first production in Pinkney Park. The inaugural show was Much Ado About Nothing — an estimated 6,000 audience members attended.

Thirty seasons later, we return to that beloved comedy under the stars, continuing our mission to produce affordable, professional open-air Shakespeare for Fairfield County.

Learn more about our history on the About page.
